issues.legal_issue: The State Government may direct a statutory housing board to disapprove an auction when the direction is necessary or expedient to carry out the purposes of the governing statute.
material_facts: The State Government disapproved the auction and directed that a fresh auction be held after reviewing information that earlier sales in the area had fetched substantially higher prices.
The direction was issued under a statutory provision empowering the State Government to give directions to the Board for carrying out the purposes of the Act and requiring the Board to comply.
issues.conclusion: The State Government was empowered to issue the direction, and the Board was required to comply with it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 60 of the Rajasthan Housing Board Act, 1970 authorizes the State Government to give the Board directions it considers necessary or expedient for carrying out the Act’s purposes, and makes compliance by the Board a duty. The provision is couched in wide language.

predicates.statutory_public_board: A public board is established under a statutory framework that subjects it to government directions.
predicates.government_direction_for_statutory_purpo: The government directs the board to take an action it considers necessary or expedient to carry out the purposes of the board’s governing law.

issues.definition: When a statutory public board receives a government direction for carrying out the purposes of its governing law, it must comply with that direction.

issues.legal_issue: A person who makes the highest bid at a public auction has no right to require completion of the sale when the auction terms reserve final acceptance of the bid and that acceptance has not occurred.
material_facts: The auction conditions reserved final authority to accept a bid to the board’s chairperson.
The respondent made the highest bid and deposited an initial amount, but the chairperson had not accepted the bid before the auction was cancelled.
issues.conclusion: The highest bidder acquired no vested right to have the auction concluded in its favour, and the High Court could not direct issuance of a demand for the balance of the price.
issues.legal_principle: The rights of a highest bidder depend on the auction conditions; where final acceptance is reserved to the public authority, no right to completion arises before acceptance. The Court relied on Laxmikant v. Satyawan, (1996) 4 SCC 208, and referred to Trilochan Mishra v. State of Orissa, (1971) 3 SCC 153, State of Orissa v. Harinarayan Jaiswal, (1972) 2 SCC 36, Union of India v. M/s Bhim Sen Walaiti Ram, (1969) 3 SCC 146, and State of Uttar Pradesh v. Vijay Bahadur Singh, (1982) 2 SCC 365.

predicates.public_auction_case: The proceeding concerns a bid made at a public auction conducted by a public authority.
predicates.final_bid_acceptance_reserved_to_authori: The auction terms reserve final acceptance or rejection of a bid to the public authority.
predicates.bid_not_finally_accepted: The public authority has not finally accepted the bidder’s offer.

issues.definition: A highest bidder at a public auction has no right to completion of the sale if the authority reserved final acceptance and has not accepted the bid.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not interfere under its writ jurisdiction with cancellation of a public auction when the decision is supported by material indicating an unfairly low price and serves the public interest in protecting public revenue.
material_facts: The auction produced a highest bid substantially below prices previously obtained for plots in the same area.
The State Government had received a report concerning bungling in the auction and disapproved it, directing a fresh auction to protect the Board’s revenue.
The High Court directed the authority to consider the bidder’s representation and issue a demand for the balance, effectively confirming the auction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have interfered with the cancellation or directed completion of the auction; its orders were set aside and the writ petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226, judicial review examines the decision-making process rather than substituting the court’s view on the merits. Review is subject to restraint, Article 14, and the need to avoid arbitrary, biased, or mala fide action; intervention in public contracts is warranted only where required by the larger public interest. The Court relied on Master Marine Services (P) Ltd. v. Metcalfe and Hodgkinson (P) Ltd., (2005) 6 SCC 138, Tata Cellular v. Union of India, (1994) 6 SCC 651, Sterling Computers Ltd. v. M/s M.N. Publications Ltd., (1993) 1 SCC 445, Raunaq International Ltd. v. I.V.R. Construction Ltd., (1999) 1 SCC 492, and Air India Ltd. v. Cochin International Airport Ltd., (2000) 2 SCC 617.

predicates.public_auction_cancellation_case: The proceeding challenges a public authority’s cancellation of an auction.
predicates.comparative_prices_show_material_underpr: Information about comparable sales indicates that the auction price was materially below prices previously obtained for similar property.
predicates.cancellation_aims_to_protect_public_reve: The authority cancels the auction and directs a fresh one to protect or increase public revenue.

issues.definition: A court should not interfere with cancellation of a public auction when comparable prices indicate material underpricing and the cancellation is aimed at protecting public revenue.

issues.legal_issue: Contempt proceedings should not continue when the authority has complied with a court direction to consider a representation by giving a hearing and deciding the representation.
material_facts: The prior court order required the authority to consider the bidder’s representation.
The authority issued notice, provided a personal hearing, and rejected the representation before the contempt order was made.
issues.conclusion: There was no occasion to initiate contempt proceedings; the contempt order was set aside and the petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Contempt proceedings were not justified because the authority had taken the steps required by the prior court direction: it gave the affected person a hearing and decided the representation.

predicates.contempt_proceeding_case: The proceeding alleges failure to comply with an earlier court direction.
predicates.prior_order_requires_representation_cons: The earlier court direction requires the authority to consider a person’s representation.
predicates.authority_heard_and_decided_representati: The authority gave the person a hearing and made a decision on the representation.

issues.definition: A contempt petition should be dismissed when the alleged noncompliance concerns a direction to consider a representation and the authority heard and decided that representation.
